title: Introduction to Digital Electronics
summary: Digital Electronics processes discrete binary signals (0 and 1) rather than continuous analog signals. It forms the backbone of modern computers, microprocessors, and digital communication systems.

images.caption: Comparison of continuous sine wave (Analog) vs discrete pulse train (Digital).

images.title: TTL Logic Levels
images.caption: Voltage thresholds for TTL: LOW (0V - 0.8V) and HIGH (2.0V - 5.0V).

working_principle: In digital systems, information is represented by two voltage levels: Logic 0 (Ground / 0V) and Logic 1 (+5V / VCC). The region between VIL(max) and VIH(min) is the noise margin region to prevent signal corruption.
advantages: High immunity to electrical noise and distortion
Easy storage and transmission of data
disadvantages: Requires Analog-to-Digital (ADC) conversion for real-world signals
Higher sampling rate requires greater bandwidth
common_mistakes: Operating inputs in the illegal indeterminate voltage zone (0.8V to 2.0V).
Assuming TTL logic levels match CMOS 3.3V logic levels.
quick_notes: Noise Margin protects against voltage fluctuations.

viva_questions.q: What is the main advantage of digital signals over analog signals?
viva_questions.a: High noise immunity and ease of processing/storage.
The maximum noise voltage that can be added to an input signal without altering the output logic state.

interview_questions.q: What happens if a TTL input receives a voltage of 1.2V?
interview_questions.a: It falls into the invalid/undefined region, causing unpredictable behavior or oscillations.
